stories.headline: Nvidia posts $96.2B quarter, up 106%, and guides to $108B with zero China compute revenue

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reported revenue of $96.221 billion for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, up 18% sequentially and 106% year over year, with GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins both at 75.0%
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the second quarter ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were both 75.0%.

key_facts.fact: Data Center revenue reached $89.0 billion, up 18% quarter over quarter and 117% year over year — growing faster than total revenue
key_facts.excerpt: Second-quarter revenue was $89.0 billion, up 18% from the previous quarter and up 117% from a year ago.

key_facts.fact: GAAP diluted EPS was $2.46 and non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.22; the company returned about $26.0 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends, with roughly $99.0 billion left under its repurchase authorization
key_facts.excerpt: GAAP diluted EPS was $2.46, while non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.22... NVIDIA returned about $26.0 billion to shareholders via repurchases and dividends in the quarter and has roughly $99.0 billion remaining under its buyback authorization.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia guided to third-quarter revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, and explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China in that outlook
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue is expected to be $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.

key_facts.fact: CFO Colette Kress said revenue should grow roughly 70% in fiscal 2028 but described that outlook as supply-constrained; gross margins are expected to bottom at 71%-72% in Q4 before settling at 72%-73% in fiscal 2028
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress said the company expects revenue to grow by approximately 70% in fiscal 2028, though she characterized that outlook as supply-constrained... Kress said gross margins are expected to bottom in the 71% to 72% range in the fourth quarter before settling at 72% to 73% in fiscal 2028 as price increases take effect.

key_facts.fact: Networking revenue hit a record, rising 18% sequentially with Spectrum-X Ethernet up 2.6x year over year; Nvidia is in full production of its Vera CPU and expects CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA's networking revenue also reached a record, increasing 18% sequentially. Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue grew 2.6 times from a year earlier, Kress said. The company also said it is in full production of its Vera CPU and expects CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028.

key_facts.fact: The $108 billion Q3 forecast came in above the roughly $104 billion analysts expected, and Nvidia expanded its AWS deal through 2028; NVDA rose more than 6%
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia forecasts Q3 revenue of $108B, above $104B est., expects FY 2028 revenue to grow by ~70%, and expands its AWS deal through 2028; NVDA jumps 6%+

stories.headline: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.9B, its biggest push into the model ecosystem

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face, the repository of open-source AI models, for $12.9 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday citing a person with knowledge of the deal
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face, a repository of open-source AI models, for $12.9 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing a person with knowledge of the deal.

key_facts.fact: A deal at that price would be one of Nvidia's largest acquisitions ever and would hand it control of the main open-source model hub just as Anthropic and OpenAI build their own chips as alternatives to Nvidia GPUs
key_facts.excerpt: It would also give Nvidia control of Hugging Face - which hosts open-source large language models and datasets - at a time when builders of closed-source models such as Anthropic and OpenAI are seeking to create their own chips as an alternative to Nvidia's graphics processing units.

key_facts.fact: The price contrasts sharply with Hugging Face's annualized revenue of about $150 million
key_facts.excerpt: The price tag would also stand in steep contrast to its annualized revenue of $150 million reported by The Information earlier this week.

key_facts.fact: Deal talks began after Hugging Face received acquisition interest from another suitor; a source told CNBC they could confirm an Nvidia acquisition 'has been part of ongoing and recent talks'
key_facts.excerpt: Deal talks began after Hugging Face, an open-source AI platform developers use to collaborate, test and share tools, received acquisition interest from another suitor, according to The Information. A source familiar with the matter told CNBC they could "confirm acquisition [by Nvidia] has been part of ongoing and recent talks."

key_facts.fact: The reported price is nearly triple Hugging Face's last known valuation of $4.5 billion, set by a $235 million round in 2023, and follows a rejected Nvidia offer to invest $500 million at a $7 billion valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Its most recent fundraise, a $235 million round in 2023 that put the company's value at $4.5 billion... Nvidia's bid to acquire Hugging Face follows a rejected offer: the chipmaker proposed a $500 million investment late last year that would have placed the company's valuation at $7 billion, which Hugging Face declined.

key_facts.fact: No signed agreement has been reached yet and the deal could still fall apart; neither Nvidia nor Hugging Face has commented publicly
key_facts.excerpt: A signed agreement has not yet been reached and the deal could still fall apart, according to TechCrunch. Business Insider reported last week that Hugging Face had been working with a bank to evaluate bidders' interest in the company.

stories.headline: SoftBank in talks to take majority control of humanoid maker 1X at a $6B valuation

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is in talks to buy a majority stake in OpenAI-backed humanoid robot developer 1X Technologies in a deal valuing the startup at about $6 billion, The Information reported Wednesday
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank is in talks to buy a majority stake in OpenAI-backed humanoid robot developer 1X Technologies in a deal that would value the startup at about $6 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the deal.

key_facts.fact: Talks are ongoing and terms could change; SoftBank and 1X did not respond to requests for comment and Reuters could not independently confirm the report
key_facts.excerpt: The talks are ongoing, and the terms could change, the report said... Reuters could not immediately confirm the report. SoftBank Group and 1X did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

key_facts.fact: The $6 billion control price is 40% below the valuation 1X itself sought: in September 2025 it told investors and employees it was seeking up to $1 billion at a valuation of at least $10 billion, and no close at that price was ever publicly confirmed
key_facts.excerpt: In September 2025, 1X told investors and employees it was seeking up to $1 billion in new funding at a valuation of at least $10 billion... A private company that pitched itself at $10 billion is being signed for 40% less, in a sector that has not slowed: humanoid-robotics startups took in $8.6 billion in the first half of 2026, according to Dealroom.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and 1X discussed a possible acquisition of 1X by the ChatGPT maker last year; OpenAI invested in 1X in 2023 through its Startup Fund alongside Tiger Global and Norwegian investors
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and 1X discussed last year the possibility of the ChatGPT-maker acquiring 1X, the report added. OpenAI invested in 1X in 2023 through its OpenAI Startup Fund, alongside Tiger Global and a group of Norway-based investors.

key_facts.fact: The deal would extend SoftBank's robotics roll-up, which already includes an agreed $5.4 billion purchase of ABB's robotics business and a $1.4 billion investment alongside Nvidia in Skild AI
key_facts.excerpt: The 1X talks are one node in a sweep that includes the signed $5.4 billion takeover of ABB's industrial robotics business, financed in part by a $1.75 billion loan package... a $1.4 billion investment alongside Nvidia in the robotics-model developer Skild AI at a valuation above $14 billion.

key_facts.fact: 1X, a Norwegian-Californian company known for its NEO home humanoid, claims more than 10,000 orders for the product
key_facts.excerpt: The Norwegian-Californian startup is known for its NEO robot and has claimed more than 10,000 orders for the product.

stories.headline: Kioxia and Sandisk commit over $31B to Japanese memory plants through 2032

key_facts.fact: Kioxia and US-based Sandisk said on Thursday they plan to invest more than $31 billion in Japan through 2032 to advance semiconductor technology and expand production capacity, as AI demand lifts memory chips
key_facts.excerpt: Japanese Kioxia and the US-based Sandisk on Thursday said they plan to invest over $31 billion in Japan through 2032 to drive semiconductor technology development expand production capacity, amid a boom in AI uptake that is boosting demand for memory chips.

key_facts.fact: The plan is contingent on government support, and its centerpiece is a new memory production facility at Kioxia's Kitakami plant in northern Japan costing 1.8 trillion yen ($11.30 billion), according to CEO Hiroo Ota
key_facts.excerpt: The investment, however, will be contingent on "government support", both companies said in a joint statement. As part of the six-year investment plan, Kioxia will build a new memory chip production facility at its Kitakami plant in northern Japan, with an investment of 1.8 trillion yen, or ($11.30 billion), Kioxia chief executive Hiroo Ota said.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia CEO Hiroo Ota and Sandisk CEO David Goeckeler met Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo on Thursday, August 27
key_facts.excerpt: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, right, poses with Sandisk Corporation CEO David Goeckeler, left, and Kioxia Corporation CEO Hiroo Ota, center, ahead of their meeting at the prime minister's office in Tokyo, Japan, Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The 5 trillion yen six-year program splits the two sites: the new Kitakami Fab3 will make high-density 3D NAND for AI servers and cloud data centers, while Yokkaichi stays focused on chips for consumer electronics such as smartphones
key_facts.excerpt: As the centerpiece of this investment, Kioxia plans to construct a third fabrication plant (Fab3) at its Kitakami site in Iwate Prefecture... The new plant in Kitakami, Iwate Prefecture, will focus on producing high-end NAND chips for data centers, while the Yokkaichi plant in Mie Prefecture will remain focused on chips for consumer electronics such as smartphones.

key_facts.fact: Kioxia and Sandisk started mass production of 10th-generation 3D flash memory at Kitakami's Fab2 in July 2026, and will apply for Japanese government subsidies for the new plant
key_facts.excerpt: In July of this year, Kioxia and SanDisk initiated mass production of 10th-generation 3D flash memory at the Kitakami plant's Fab2 (K2)... In addition, Kioxia and SanDisk will apply for government subsidies from Japan for the construction of the new plant.

key_facts.fact: Sandisk shares rose more than 4% in pre-market trading after the announcement; the two companies have partnered on flash memory for over 25 years
key_facts.excerpt: Following the news, SanDisk shares rose over 4% in pre-market trading... The collaboration between these two companies spans over 25 years, underscoring a deep-rooted partnership in the semiconductor hardware sector.

stories.headline: US probes freight forwarder Apex Logistics over Nvidia AI servers routed into China

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Aug 27 that the United States is investigating Singapore-based Apex Logistics over its suspected role in supplying Nvidia AI chips to China
key_facts.excerpt: Bloomberg had earlier on Aug 27 reported that the United States was investigating Apex over its suspected role in supplying AI chips to China, citing sources familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Apex Logistics is wholly owned by Swiss logistics giant Kuehne+Nagel, whose spokesperson told The Straits Times on Aug 27 that Apex 'is fully cooperating with the relevant authorities regarding this isolated matter within a wider US government investigation'
key_facts.excerpt: In a response to The Straits Times on Aug 27, a Kuehne+Nagel spokesperson confirmed that "Apex Logistics is fully cooperating with the relevant authorities regarding this isolated matter within a wider US government investigation".

key_facts.fact: The suspected route ran Nvidia-powered AI servers from Taiwan to the US, then to an Asian destination outside China, then to Hong Kong, from where they were driven into mainland China; US investigators are focused on the US-to-Southeast-Asia leg
key_facts.excerpt: the smuggling routes that the US suspects Apex may have facilitated involve the transportation of Nvidia-powered AI servers from Taiwan to the US, then to an Asian destination outside of China, before delivery to Hong Kong. The sources said the servers were then driven from Hong Kong into mainland China.

key_facts.fact: Apex told Bloomberg it was aware of US 'concern for and interest in a small number of shipments that Apex handled in 2024 and which may have involved materials and equipment which were ultimately forwarded to prohibited locations'
key_facts.excerpt: Apex said in a statement to Bloomberg that it was aware of the US' "concern for and interest in a small number of shipments that Apex handled in 2024 and which may have involved materials and equipment which were ultimately forwarded to prohibited locations".

key_facts.fact: Washington has restricted sales of high-end AI chips to China since 2022, including more recently the China-specific H20; Singapore PM Lawrence Wong said on Aug 23 the country will not be used as a conduit for illegal trade but cannot verify every supply chain
key_facts.excerpt: Washington has since 2022 put restrictions on the sale of high-end AI chips to China, including more recently on H20 chips designed specifically for the market... Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said during the National Day Rally on Aug 23 that the Republic will not allow itself to be used as a conduit for illegal trade practices, but nor can it possibly trace and verify the entire supply chain behind every product that passes through its shores.

stories.headline: Hugging Face unveils Microduck, a $399 open-source biped you train with reinforcement learning

key_facts.fact: Pollen Robotics, Hugging Face's robotics arm, launched the Microduck on Aug 27: a one-eyed biped just under 10 inches tall, available to preorder for $399 in four colors, with shipping promised 'before Christmas 2026'
key_facts.excerpt: Hugging Face's Pollen Robotics has launched its second cute AI robot, the Microduck, a one-eyed biped standing just under 10 inches tall. It's available to preorder now for $399 in cream, graphite, lavender, and sky blue, and Pollen Robotics says it plans to start shipping the little robot "before Christmas 2026."

key_facts.fact: The robot runs on a Rockchip RK3566 processor and carries a camera, motion sensors, LiDAR and articulated legs, head and neck; demos show it picking up socks and markers, kicking a ball and moving on tiny rollerskates
key_facts.excerpt: It runs on a Rockchip RK3566 processor and has a camera, motion sensors, LiDAR, and articulated legs, head, and neck... Video demos of the Microduck show it picking up socks and markers, kicking around a ball, and zipping around on tiny rollerskates.

key_facts.fact: Behaviours are learned in physics simulation — on the owner's machine or on Hugging Face Jobs — and the SDK, simulation and full reinforcement-learning training stack are published on GitHub
key_facts.excerpt: Behaviours are learned in physics sim, on your machine or on Hugging Face Jobs... The SDK, the simulation and the full RL training stack are on GitHub. What the robot runs is what you can read, fork and retrain.

key_facts.fact: Pollen Robotics describes it as a 25 cm open-source biped you train with reinforcement learning, playable out of the box, with the kit including 3 spare motors, 2 batteries, a dual charger, 10 NFC tags and Hugging Face credit
key_facts.excerpt: 25 cm open-source b[iped]... with reinforcement learning. Playable out of the box... 3x spare motors, 5x motor cables, 2x batteries, dual charger, 10x NFC tags, Hugging Face credit, screwdriver, screw pack.

key_facts.fact: Each unit generates its own audio identity the first time it wakes up and keeps that voice for life, communicating through sounds Pollen says are 'closer to a creature than an assistant'
key_facts.excerpt: "it communicates through weird little sounds, closer to a creature than an assistant. Each Microduck gets its own audio identity the first time it wakes up, tied to that individual robot so it keeps the same voice for life."

key_facts.fact: It is Hugging Face's second robot after Reachy Mini, and was developed in part by Pollen Robotics, the Bordeaux, France-based company Hugging Face acquired last year
key_facts.excerpt: It will go on sale later this year, Hugging Face said Thursday, making it the second robot from the company... The robot was developed in part by Pollen Robotics, the Bordeaux, France-based company Hugging Face acquired last year.

key_facts.fact: Pollen Robotics announced it on X: 'We built a small biped robot you can teach new tricks to. Train it in simulation, run it on the real thing. Meet Microduck'
key_facts.excerpt: We built a small biped robot you can teach new tricks to. Train it in simulation, run it on the real thing. Meet Microduck

stories.headline: White House weighs chip tariffs that would also hit laptops, consoles and data-center servers

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration is considering a new round of sweeping semiconductor tariffs, Politico reported Thursday citing eight people familiar with the discussions
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration is considering a new round of sweeping tariffs on semiconductors, Politico reported on Thursday citing eight people familiar with discussions.

key_facts.fact: Rather than taxing only microchips, the duties would extend to products that use them — laptops, gaming consoles and data center servers
key_facts.excerpt: A new tariff proposal could tax a wider range of tech goods. Instead of just targeting microchips, the duties would also apply to products that use them, such as laptops, gaming consoles, and data center servers, the report said.

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick favors a structure tying foreign companies' relief from the tariffs to how much they invest in US chip manufacturing; officials are also weighing a phase-in period and country-specific rates and import quotas
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick favors a structure that will tie foreign companies' relief from the tariffs to investment in U.S. chip manufacturing to boost local production, the report said. Washington is also mulling a phase-in period and the framework could still be substantially revised in the coming weeks or months.

key_facts.fact: The White House told Politico that 'Reshoring semiconductor manufacturing is a top priority for President Trump, whose policies have already secured hundreds of billions of dollars of investments in this key sector'
key_facts.excerpt: The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC, but told Politico: "Reshoring semiconductor manufacturing is a top priority for President Trump, whose policies have already secured hundreds of billions of dollars of investments in this key sector."

key_facts.fact: The administration already imposed a 25% tariff on certain AI chips in January; Trump had earlier floated roughly 100% tariffs on semiconductors with exemptions for domestic manufacturing, which never materialized
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said last year that he was planning to unveil new tariffs on semiconductors and chips, but the measures didn't materialize. The president also said at the time that he intends to impose tariffs of "approximately 100%" on semiconductors and chips, but there will be no charge for companies building domestically. In January, the Trump administration did impose a 25% tariff on certain AI chips.

key_facts.fact: Industry representatives warned that broader tariffs could raise the cost of data center construction, slow US investment in AI infrastructure and lift prices for servers, computers and televisions
key_facts.excerpt: Industry representatives have warned that broader tariffs could increase the cost of data center construction, slow US investment in AI infrastructure, and raise prices for servers, computers, televisions, and other electronic products.
